messages:
Sara (oncall): heads-up — after yesterday's paging mess I want to propose some concrete postmortem automation changes. short thread to collect ideas. :wave:
Kevin (SRE): yes please. main pain was having to manually create the postmortem doc + link the customer impact table. took ~40m while oncall.
Maria (EngPM): agreed. also we missed a couple of action items because they were just @mentioned in the thread and not tracked anywhere.
Josh (infra): +1. my notes: create postmortem skeleton from incident metadata, auto-populate severity, start/end times, services, pager history, and affected customers.
Sara (oncall): exactly. thinking: IncidentBot should offer a "Create postmortem" button in the thread that spins up the doc, links the incident id, and opens the action-item tracker.
IncidentBot: Incident 842 detected. Severity: P1. Affected service: inference-runtime. Pager history: 3 pages. Would you like to: [Create postmortem] [Mark as no-postmortem]
Maria (EngPM): UX idea: when the PM or SRE clicks create, it should prompt for initial customer impact estimate (minor/moderate/major) and attach the relevant customer list from the incident tags. Saves time.
Kevin (SRE): +auto-fill. Also add a field for "mitigation timeline" auto-generated from the oncall runbook logs. We can extract key events via the pagerbot events.
Josh (infra): tech note — we can implement a small lambda that pulls the incident protobuf and fills a Notion template via API. snippet for the action:
```
POST /notion/v1/pages
{
  "parent": {"database_id": "PM-Postmortems"},
  "properties": {"Incident": "842", "Severity": "P1", "Service": "inference-runtime"},
  "children": [ ... ]
}
```
Liz (Product): we need to make sure customer-impact labels map to CS tags so Support can prioritize comms. e.g., if "major" => create a sales-notify task.
Sara (oncall): flow idea:
1) Incident resolves or is snoozed -> IncidentBot posts resolution summary + CTA to create postmortem.
2) Click -> prefilled doc + checklist for who owns first draft, expected due date, and initial action items with owners.
3) Create action items automatically in our tracker (Jira/Linear) tagged with incident id and due dates.
4) Auto-schedule a 30m review meeting if participants haven't assigned owner in 24h.

Kevin (SRE): For action items: enforce SLA-based reminders (e.g., 24h ack, 7d fix plan, 30d completion). Could be reminders via Slack DM from InfraBot.
InfraBot: scheduled reminder created: "PM-Postmortem-842 — ack due in 24h" (reminder ID: r-842-a1) :calendar:
Maria (EngPM): we should have a small table of "incident -> customer impact -> postmortem requirement" so not every incident generates a full postmortem. i can help draft thresholds.
Josh (infra): technical detail: include an audit log entry linking the postmortem doc to the infra logs snapshot (s3 path) and a KV of the exact git commit hash for runtime deploys.
Sara (oncall): one more: make the on-call handoff easier. If an incident spans shifts, IncidentBot should summarize what still needs ownership in the handoff message and surface open actions.
Maria (EngPM): +1 — handoffs were messy yesterday. also include the list of affected customers and current comms drafts in that summary.
Kevin (SRE): small RFC idea: add a lightweight template for "rapid postmortem" where the bot auto-classifies routine incidents and creates a short 3-section doc (what happened, mitigation, actions) — only escalates to full PM if customer-impact is high.
Liz (Product): love that. reduces noise and ensures high-impact get full reviews.
Sara (oncall): on the automation side, can we wire the following commands into IncidentBot?
- `/incident create-pm 842 --template rapid`
- `/incident pm-assign 842 @kevin @maria --due 2026-04-01`
- `/incident pm-status 842`

Josh (infra): yep. we can add slash commands and a tiny backend that talks to Notion + Jira + our action-item dashboard.
Kevin (SRE): actionable priorities for next sprint:
- IncidentBot: Create postmortem button + prefill (owner: infra)
- Action item automation: create tracker item in Jira/Linear with SLA reminders (owner: SRE infra)
- Handoff summary: include outstanding actions + comms (owner: oncall tooling)
- Customer-impact mapping doc (owner: product)

Sara (oncall): can someone volunteer to own the IncidentBot PR? small change to add buttons + callouts.
Josh (infra): I can take the PR. will open branch and prototype the Notion payload.
Maria (EngPM): I'll draft the threshold doc for which incidents need a full postmortem and a sample rapid-template.
Kevin (SRE): I'll sketch the SLA reminder flow and InfraBot reminder hooks.
Liz (Product): I'll handle the mapping to CS and sales-notify flows.
Sara (oncall): perfect. let's add these as action items in this thread so we don't lose them. InfraBot, create the actions in Jira/Linear with due dates of 1 week for prototypes.
InfraBot: Creating tasks: PM-Postmortem-842-CreateButton (assignee: Josh) due 2026-03-22; PM-Postmortem-842-ThresholdDoc (assignee: Maria) due 2026-03-22; PM-Postmortem-842-ReminderFlow (assignee: Kevin) due 2026-03-22; PM-Postmortem-842-CSLink (assignee: Liz) due 2026-03-22.
Sara (oncall): thanks. i'll follow up in next oncall sync. if anyone sees edge cases (air-gapped private customers, on-prem incidents), ping here.
Kevin (SRE): noted — on-prem incidents need a slightly different flow (no Notion API). we'll fallback to internal S3 + doc generator.
Maria (EngPM): added one more ask: expose a single dashboard view that shows all open postmortems, status, open actions, and customer impact so Eng/Product can triage. maybe a Grafana or simple React page.
Josh (infra): we'll prototype a small "postmortem HQ" with APIs from Notion/Jira/our logs service.
Sara (oncall): great work team. thanks for quick volunteers. :thumbsup:
Liz (Product): :eyes: will review the assumptions and jump on any follow-ups.
IncidentBot: Note: this thread generated 4 tasks and a prototype owner list. Use `/incident pm-status 842` to see progress.
Sara (oncall): closing the thread for now — will reopen when prototypes land. if anyone wants to add follow-ups, reply here.
